title: Fly over Naltar, Pakistan's ski valley
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: North of Gilgit, a side valley climbs into the Karakoram mountains. This is Naltar.
We start over the Hunza River, and then turn west, into the valley.
Naltar is about forty kilometres from Gilgit, but the last part of the road is a rough jeep track along the Naltar River.
The valley is lined with thick pine forests, rare in this dry and rocky part of Gilgit-Baltistan.
There are two main villages: Naltar Payan, the lower village, and Naltar Bala, the upper one.
In winter, Naltar becomes one of Pakistan's few ski resorts. The Pakistan Air Force runs the slopes, and hosts national championships here.
A chairlift was installed in twenty fourteen, running from the Air Force base camp towards Bargo Pass.
Skiers from Pakistan have competed at the Winter Olympics, including Muhammad Abbas in twenty ten, and Muhammad Karim in twenty fourteen.
Higher up, the Naltar lakes, also called the Bashkiri lakes, shine in shades of green, blue and turquoise.
In summer, the meadows fill with flowers, and visitors come for trekking, camping and fishing.
Many families here farm small plots, and grow potatoes once a year. Many others work at the ski resort.
